title: backlog.py reads backlog.json from the tool's own root at import, so with --root another project only config and check use that project's settings
goal: Every backlog.py command run with --root PROJECT (or from a project whose root differs from the tool's) reads PROJECT's backlog.json (or KB_BACKLOG_CONFIG) for every setting: bl_base's import-time read (_LOADED = read_settings(ROOT)) and the module constants made from it (REL_DIR, KINDS, ID_RE, ALWAYS_IN_SCOPE, the land steps, WORKER_DIR, ID_SHAPE) follow the root the command runs on, so new, set, check, land, brief and dispatch use the project's item_dir, id prefixes, trackers and worktree_dir; bl_ci.in_worker_worktree reads worktree_dir instead of a literal; the kb's own behaviour is unchanged; no bl_ module imports backlog or kbgit. Found by the SP-befc6yqr review (gap S1 of ST-qgnjxiol).

gates.question: How do the commands follow the project root's settings instead of the tool root's import-time read?
options: settings are loaded once per process for the root the command runs on (bl_cli's main, from --root or the working tree's git root, before any command), and every reader takes them at call time through bl_base accessors, never through a constant copied at import
keep the import-time constants and rebind them in every loaded bl_ module after --root is parsed
gates.recommendation: settings are loaded once per process for the root the command runs on (bl_cli's main, from --root or the working tree's git root, before any command), and every reader takes them at call time through bl_base accessors, never through a constant copied at import
